reason: Verified in source and in the running page. render-b.js editor() builds exactly one input (#b-edit-title) plus four .b-step buttons (-7,-1,+1,+7) and a read-only .b-stepRead status line; setAway() is the only writer of an item's position and is only ever called from a stepper click or undo(). Driving ?v=approach&state=owner-editing confirms it: one input, labels 'What it is' / 'When' / 'What guests see', readout 'Saturday 8 August 2026 in 23 days', and three +7 presses to reach 44 days. There is no drag, no arrow-key nudge on the row, and no absolute-date path anywhere in the owner surface, so rescheduling to a named date is head arithmetic on the one surface built to remove it. The self-contradiction is real too: owner-empty renders a mono text input placeholdered '3 October 2026' behind 'Set the day', so typed absolute dates are already the product's language, just not where moments are actually moved. This is not a gate restatement (interaction-check.mjs asserts nothing about typed dates), not taste, and the fix adds no colour, weight or family.
sharpenedFix: Real, but the fix as written aims slightly wrong in three places. (1) Do not seed the field with F.fmt.longYear(iso) — 'Saturday 8 August 2026' is a value a user has to delete a weekday out of before typing. Seed with the day-month-year form (parts.day + ' ' + parts.month + ' ' + parts.year) and let the parser tolerate an optional leading weekday and an omitted year (assume the nearest forward year). fixture.js has no parser today, only formatters, so add one small F.parseDay(text) -> iso|null beside fmt in fixture.js rather than inlining date logic in render-b.js. (2) Route the commit through setAway(root, item, daysFrom(clock, iso)) with the same clock the steppers read (item.parentElement's data-clock), so the ceiling clamp, the .b-away / .b-date / .b-grab aria-label rewrite, the .b-ceiling note and place() all stay on the single-writer path; push {id,title,from,to} onto history and call paintUndo only when to !== from, exactly as step() does. (3) Refusal must cover three cases, not one: unparseable, on or before the clock date (setAway floors at 1, so a past date would silently snap and lie), and after the primary date. Give each its own hint text in the existing b-hint pattern (aria-invalid, role=status, focus kept) rather than one generic 'Pick the date, or use the steppers'. Commit on Enter and on blur, not on a new button — the editor already closes with 'Done' and a fourth control in the When group would crowd it. Add interaction-check assertions for: typed date moves the row and lands in history; a date past the day itself is refused and leaves data-away unchanged; the readout and the row's date line agree after a typed commit.
